mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the prior three months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE is below 4% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue growth for consumer-facing firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative following two consecutive quarterly declines in GDPC1.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average by more than 2% for three consecutive months signals a supply-side expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when INDPRO exceeds its 12-month MA by more than 2% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their 12-month averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and erodes equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average by more than 1% in a single month, combined with a concurrent decline in the unemployment rate, signals a rapidly tightening labor market that increases wage growth and input costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-mo MA +1% AND UNRATE falls in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both conditions are met in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 6-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a recovery in residential construction demand, which boosts materials and homebuilding sector earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST is above its 6-month moving average for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) below their 12-month averages for two consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in demand, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < 12-mo MA AND HOUST < 12-mo MA for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST are below their 12-month averages for two consecutive months.
